threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'Poppy' in the corner shop is just for smoke. You can spot a local a mile off just by their understanding of that place's true vibe.
Caught a couple arguing loudly about a lost shoe on the 45 last night. One of them was wearing neon green socks. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw that guy planting flowers in a traffic island while the bus drivers debated strike plans over coffee nearby.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand next to a vintage record shop, where the aroma of grilled meat mixes with classic vinyl. It's a vibe!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their calm when a BART meltdown happens—while the newcomers freak out, we just roll our eyes and plan for the next bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus after a BART delay. He stopped mid-act to help an elderly woman with her grocery bags. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas, but locals go for the bocadillos—more filling and way less overhyped.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their frantic search for a 'menú del día' in the fanciest spots, completely missing the hidden gems in the back streets.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus is reliable. Locals know it’s just a gentle suggestion from TfL.
Caught a group on the 59 last night debating if pineapple belongs on pizza. One guy went on about it for 20 minutes, while the driver just rolled his eyes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a street musician playing an accordion outside the Späti while the scent of fresh kebab wafted through the air.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop and a craft beer bar sharing the same building, both thriving at 3 AM on a Tuesday.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively roll their eyes at tourists blocking the sidewalk while trying to take selfies with the murals.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus the other day with a guy playing violin, and it felt like a mini concert. Just another day in the Tenderloin, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think all bars close at 2 AM, but in Gràcia, you'll find some open well past dawn, still buzzing with locals and laughter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over T10 ticket limits—I've seen tourists line up at machines for 20 minutes trying to figure it out.
